definition: Commemorate means to honor and keep alive the memory of a past event or person — usually with a ceremony, an anniversary, or a lasting marker.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word commemorate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know commemorate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The library commemorates its founder each October by displaying her battered reading journal under glass.
Acknowledge is weaker than commemorate: acknowledging a past event just notes that it happened, while commemorating it builds ceremony and care around its memory.
Enshrine goes further than commemorate: a commemorated event is remembered with ceremonies, but an enshrined one is fixed permanently in place — set apart as almost sacred.

Honor means to show public, formal respect, and you can honor someone living, present, and sitting in the room. Commemorate is honor aimed at memory: it keeps a past event or person from being forgotten, usually on an anniversary or with a lasting marker.

Memorialize means to preserve a memory in permanent form — a statue, a plaque, a renamed bridge. Commemorate is broader: a single ceremony, a moment of silence, or an annual reading can commemorate what no permanent object marks.
